ROOT_CAUSE:
The dispatch was not blocked. It had already gone out, and the verifier recorded it as a failure.

The one DISPATCH_MARCH attempt the ledger has ever recorded (2026-10-02T09:24:28Z, rev 3ce3ef3) carries both states, and they answer the question the order asked: before page=MARCH marches=[] march_used=None, after page=MAP marches=['MARCHING'] march_used=1. A march began between two frames of a step whose tap was delivered (executor_backend MAA), so the game accepted the dispatch -- and the row says FAILURE. The run then walked the whole search/gather/clear flow again (steps 17-20) toward a second one.

Seven of the eight sub-conditions of STALE_OR_ROLE_UNSCOPED_FORMATION held on that frame. The only one that failed was `formation.resource_type ("WOOD") == before.resource_target ("MEAT")`, and `resource_target` was MEAT from step 7 to step 20 of that episode -- never WOOD. The WOOD came from two fabrications meeting in one comparison:

  * `vision.py` synthesised `WorldState(page=Page.MARCH, resource_target="WOOD")` from the dispatch button's template. The picture never said WOOD: the formation page prints its resource in its header (the archived frame reads 生肉), and no declared record reads that header -- measured with the production stack on the four frames of that episode, all four return `resource_target == "WOOD"`. Its siblings in the same if-chain claim only what their templates evidence.
  * `_annotate_gather_formation` froze that value into the formation record, falling back to `self._active_gather_resource` -- a memory of another goal's plan, set only while the GATHER_RESOURCE goal runs, and this episode's goal was ALLIANCE_TIMED_EVENTS.

So the clause compared a fabrication against a plan, and could not pass for any resource but the placeholder. Because it short-circuited the role-scope test, the policy underneath was never evaluated at all -- which is also why the loop kept clearing heroes blindly. Replayed through the real policy on the recorded formations, the run had been doing exactly the right thing:

    step 14  policy(MEAT) -> CLEANUP_REQUIRED remove_slots=[2, 3]   it cleared 2 and 3
    step 15  policy(MEAT) -> CLEANUP_REQUIRED remove_slots=[3]      it cleared 3
    step 16  policy(MEAT) -> READY_WITH_SPECIALIST remove_slots=[]  ...and the verifier refused

The cost is one march recorded as a failure plus four steps re-walking the flow, and the same shape recurs every time the flow reaches that hop.

REMAINING_ISSUE:
Five.

(a) The live effect is unobserved (see VERIFIER_RESULT).

(b) The gather path still has no resource fact from the frame: the formation page's header (生肉/木材/煤炭/铁矿) is a picture no declared record reads, so resource_source can only ever be PLANNED today and the clause can only report NOT_STATED_BY_PAGE. Handed on as WB-1002-18 with the corpus requirement written into it (>=10 frames, four resources -- not a single-frame ROI).

(c) The verifier's after side accepts ANY march: page=MAP plus a MARCHING/GATHERING row at all plus a global march_used >= 1, none of which is this tap's. That is the mirror-image false positive of the false negative fixed here, and on the recorded row it is invisible only because the march genuinely did belong to the tap. Handed on as WB-1002-19.

(d) `vision.py` still invents resource_target="WOOD" on one MAP state (the march-counter reader). Left alone deliberately: that page has more consumers than the two changed here, and the honest move was to measure them rather than bundle the change. Recorded as a finding.

(e) The verifier asks only that the formation's role_id be non-empty, never that it be ours -- it has no independent statement of ours to compare against. On a real frame the observed_at == before.timestamp clause is what covers it (a record read under another role cannot carry this frame's timestamp), but that is an argument, not a check. Written into test_hero_portraits rather than left implicit, because the test that appeared to cover cross-role was in fact being covered by the resource comparison.
